title: Canary metrics blitz — standup notes and action log
content:
Attendees: Avery (lead), Marco, Priya, Samir, Elena, QA: Jordan
Meeting length: 30m sync + 20m ad-hoc triage
Context: Rapid canary rollout of per-route rollout scoring and UI flag that toggles automatic fallback heuristics. Yesterday we saw a small but consistent uptick in end-to-end tail latency (p95) for the new analytic instrumentation. This blitz is to align quick fixes, measurement adjustments, and to own next 48h tasks.

Summary of current state:
- Canary cohort: 12% of traffic for 'rollout-v2' across NA region; backup route configured to model-v1-quantized.
- Observed regressions since 2026-04-27 18:00 UTC: p95 increased from 310ms -> 470ms on the console list view when sampling is enabled. Token-level CPU spikes correlate with a batching threshold change.
- Errors: rare 502s (~0.02%), mostly on long-poll websocket sessions to the streaming tier.
- Analytics delta: metric-card render time increased by ~120ms (median) when the new per-route scoring call is made inline.

Hypotheses (short):
1) Instrumentation call added to render path is blocking rendering on slow responses (Priya).
2) Batching policy now emits a smaller number of larger batches under certain seq-len distributions causing kernel contention (Marco).
3) Fallthrough to fallback model adds an extra network hop for some paths under bursty traffic (Samir).

Immediate actions agreed (owners + due):
- Priya: Push a quick experiment to switch the scoring call to async fire-and-forget on the client side for the canary cohort. Add a lightweight queue with 200ms buffer. (Jira: RINF-2381-1) Due 2026-04-29 12:00 UTC.
- Marco: Revert batching tweak from PR #1398 for canary nodes and re-run perf harness; collect per-GPU kernel time breakdown. (GH: pull/1412) Due 2026-04-29 18:00 UTC.
- Samir: Add a short-circuit so that fallback routing is only attempted after a 150ms local timeout (avoid extra hop for sub-threshold cases). Deploy to canary as feature flag. (Jira: RINF-2381-2) Due 2026-04-29 09:00 UTC.
- Elena (observability): Add a dedicated dashboard tile for the canary p95 with a stream of example request ids showing stack (trace + events). Configure alert if p95 delta > 100ms vs control for 5m. Due 2026-04-28 EOD.
- Jordan (QA): Smoke tests for websocket streaming with the deferred scoring flow; record error counts and time-to-first-payload. Due 2026-04-30.

Data and measurement notes:
- Use both synthetic harness (local traffic generator) and production sampled traces. We will compare three cohorts: control (no scoring), canary A (inline scoring), canary B (async scoring).
- Primary metrics: client p95 render, model request p95, streaming time-to-first-payload, 502 rate. Secondary: cost per token, batching efficiency (tokens/batch), queue depth.
- Sampling: add header X-Canary-Test with values control|inline|async for easier filtering at the ingestion layer.

Open questions / risks:
- Will async scoring introduce eventual consistency issues for analytics dashboards that depend on immediate scoring? (Product tradeoff)
- Does reverting the batching change degrade throughput at high concurrency? Need throughput vs latency curve.
- Is the 150ms short-circuit safe for international regions with higher base RTTs? (regional threshold tuning needed)

Decisions made:
- Temporary decision to favor user-facing latency over immediate scoring accuracy for 48h while we triage.
- Deployments will use feature flags at the service side so rollout can be toggled per-subnet.

Follow-ups and sync plan:
- Quick sync tomorrow 09:00 PT to review initial telemetry from async scoring experiment. Add 10m at the start of daily standup.
- Friday demo: Marco to present kernel breakdown charts in the weekly eng all-hands.
- Add a post-mortem if canary p95 does not return to baseline within 72h; timeline and scope owned by Avery.

Misc notes (brain-dump):
- Consider adding client-side render skeleton if scoring is slow — show cached prior score while async refresh comes back.
- Investigate whether prefix KV cache interaction increases seq-len for certain user flows causing abnormal batching.

Action log (concise):
- RINF-2381-1: async scoring client experiment — Priya — 2026-04-29 12:00
- RINF-2381-2: fallback short-circuit guard — Samir — 2026-04-29 09:00
- RINF-2381-3: revert batching tweak in canary — Marco — 2026-04-29 18:00
- RINF-2381-4: canary p95 dashboard + alert — Elena — 2026-04-28 EOD
- RINF-2381-5: websocket smoke & regression tests — Jordan — 2026-04-30

If you're blocked or need access to canary logs, add the tag #canary-blitz in the Slack thread or ping Avery directly.

End of notes.
